subject: hist
source: Cambridge IGCSE History (0470) syllabus for examination in 2027 and 2028 — Cambridge International; Core Option B (international relations since 1919, key questions 1–3) and Depth Study B (Germany, 1918–45); option choices assumed as the most common school pathway

weeks.topic: Historical skills: sources, provenance and IGCSE question types
objectives: Identify origin, purpose and audience of a source
Distinguish knowledge recall from explanation and evaluation questions

weeks.topic: The aims of the Big Three at the Paris Peace Conference, 1919
objectives: Compare the aims of Wilson, Clemenceau and Lloyd George
Explain the Fourteen Points

weeks.topic: Why the victors did not get everything they wanted
objectives: Explain conflicts between the aims of the Big Three
Assess who was most satisfied with the settlement

weeks.topic: The terms of the Treaty of Versailles
objectives: Describe the territorial, military and financial terms
Explain the War Guilt clause (Article 231)

weeks.topic: The impact of the Treaty of Versailles on Germany to 1923
objectives: Explain German reactions and the 'diktat'
Describe the Ruhr occupation and hyperinflation of 1923

weeks.topic: Was the Treaty of Versailles fair? Contemporary justifications
objectives: Evaluate arguments that the Treaty was too harsh or justified
Use contemporary sources and cartoons to support a judgement

weeks.topic: The League of Nations: aims, organisation and membership weaknesses
objectives: Describe the aims and structure of the League
Explain weaknesses such as US absence and lack of an army

weeks.topic: League peacekeeping in the 1920s
objectives: Assess League success in the Aaland Islands, Upper Silesia, Corfu and Bulgaria
Explain the role of the Locarno Treaties and Kellogg–Briand Pact

weeks.topic: The humanitarian work of the League and the ILO
objectives: Describe work on refugees, health, slavery and working conditions
Evaluate the importance of the League's agencies

weeks.topic: The Depression and the League: the Manchurian crisis
objectives: Explain how the Depression weakened the League
Analyse the League's response to Japan's invasion of Manchuria

weeks.topic: The Abyssinian crisis and the collapse of the League
objectives: Explain the League's failure over Abyssinia
Assess the Hoare–Laval Pact and sanctions

weeks.topic: Long-term effects of the peace settlement on the 1930s
objectives: Explain how resentment of Versailles fuelled extremism
Assess the link between Versailles and the outbreak of war

weeks.topic: Hitler's aims and early foreign policy: rearmament, the Saar and the Rhineland
objectives: Describe Hitler's foreign policy aims including Lebensraum
Explain rearmament and the remilitarisation of the Rhineland

weeks.topic: The Anschluss and the Sudeten crisis: the Munich Agreement
objectives: Describe the union with Austria in 1938
Explain the Sudeten crisis and the Munich Agreement

weeks.topic: Review: the peace settlement, the League of Nations and Hitler's early foreign policy
objectives: Revisit key events and dates
Practise structured questions on Versailles and the League

weeks.topic: Appeasement: was it justified?
objectives: Explain reasons for appeasement
Evaluate arguments for and against Chamberlain's policy

weeks.topic: The Nazi–Soviet Pact and the invasion of Poland
objectives: Explain why Hitler and Stalin signed the Pact
Describe the invasion of Poland in September 1939

weeks.topic: Why Britain and France declared war in 1939: how far was Hitler to blame?
objectives: Explain the British and French declarations of war
Write a balanced essay weighing Hitler against other causes

weeks.topic: Depth study Germany: the birth of the Weimar Republic and its constitution
objectives: Describe the end of the Kaiser's rule and the November Revolution
Evaluate strengths and weaknesses of the Weimar constitution

weeks.topic: Weimar crises, 1919–23: Spartacists, Kapp Putsch and hyperinflation
objectives: Describe threats from left and right
Explain the causes and effects of hyperinflation

weeks.topic: Stresemann and the recovery of the Weimar Republic, 1924–29
objectives: Explain the Rentenmark, Dawes Plan and Young Plan
Assess the 'Golden Age' of Weimar

weeks.topic: Hitler and the early Nazi Party; the Munich Putsch
objectives: Describe the origins of the Nazi Party
Explain the Munich Putsch and its consequences
Describe Mein Kampf

weeks.topic: The Depression and the rise of Nazi support, 1929–32
objectives: Explain the impact of the Wall Street Crash on Germany
Analyse the reasons for growing Nazi electoral support

weeks.topic: How Hitler became Chancellor in January 1933
objectives: Explain the political intrigue of Papen, Schleicher and Hindenburg
Assess why Hitler was appointed

weeks.topic: Consolidation of power: the Reichstag Fire and the Enabling Act
objectives: Explain the significance of the Reichstag Fire
Describe the Enabling Act and the banning of parties and trade unions

weeks.topic: The Night of the Long Knives and Hitler as Führer, 1934
objectives: Explain why Hitler purged the SA
Describe the army oath and Hitler becoming Führer

weeks.topic: Mid-year exams: Versailles to 1939 and Germany to 1934
objectives: Answer structured and source questions under timed conditions
Review feedback on essay structure

weeks.topic: Nazi control: the SS, Gestapo, courts and terror
objectives: Describe the police state and concentration camps
Assess the effectiveness of terror

weeks.topic: Propaganda and censorship under Goebbels
objectives: Describe methods of propaganda in media, rallies and culture
Evaluate how far propaganda won support

weeks.topic: Opposition and resistance: churches, youth groups and the July Bomb Plot
objectives: Describe Nazi policies towards the Catholic and Protestant churches
Assess the extent of opposition

weeks.topic: The Nazi economy: employment, autobahns and rearmament
objectives: Explain how unemployment was reduced
Describe the role of Schacht, Göring and the Four-Year Plan

weeks.topic: Women and the family in Nazi Germany
objectives: Describe Nazi views on women's roles
Explain policies such as the Law for the Encouragement of Marriage

weeks.topic: Youth and education: the Hitler Youth and Nazi schools
objectives: Describe the Hitler Youth and League of German Maidens
Explain changes to the school curriculum

weeks.topic: Persecution of minorities: the Nuremberg Laws and Kristallnacht
objectives: Describe racial ideology and persecution of Jews and other groups
Explain the Nuremberg Laws and Kristallnacht

weeks.topic: Life in wartime Germany, 1939–45
objectives: Describe rationing, total war and bombing
Outline the Final Solution

weeks.topic: End-of-year exams: international relations 1919–39 and Germany 1918–45
objectives: Complete core and depth-study papers
Apply source-analysis skills to unseen documents

weeks.topic: Review: Nazi control and life in Nazi Germany
objectives: Correct errors from end-of-year exams
Consolidate key dates and terms before Year 11
